name: default
description: Question-answering over the sample corpus, used to measure how much downstream answer accuracy survives compression. Contexts are shared between items so each is compressed once per run.

log_incident.description: The incident window of the checkout service log. A slice rather than the full 107k-token file because the A/B test requires the *uncompressed* context to fit the downstream model's window - the full file does not. Compression ratio on the whole file is reported separately.

postmortem.description: Full incident postmortem. Prose with almost no redundancy - the hardest case for a compressor.

auth_code.description: Authentication service source. Tests whether compressed code stays answerable.

tickets.description: Customer support tickets, heavily duplicated in meaning but not in wording.

items.question: Which configuration value caused the incident, and what value was it resolved to?
items.expected_answer: PAYMENT_POOL_SIZE was resolved to 8, because the deployment manifest override was absent.

items.question: What exception type was raised in the charge path, and against which host?
How long did gateway calls wait before timing out?
Which version was the rollback target?
What was the recorded connection pool wait time, and what were the pool's in-use and size values when it was exceeded?
What did p99 latency for POST /v1/checkout rise from, and to what?
How many checkout attempts were affected and what was the estimated revenue impact?
items.expected_answer: About 14,200 attempts were affected, with an estimated $86,000 revenue impact.

items.question: Why were no duplicate charges issued to customers during the incident?
items.expected_answer: The payment client uses idempotency keys on every charge request.

items.question: What is action item A-1 and which team owns it?
items.expected_answer: Add an alert on pool_wait_ms p99 above 500 ms, owned by Platform.

items.question: What algorithm and iteration count are used to hash passwords?
How long is an access token valid for, in seconds?
What is the maximum length allowed for a password, and how does it differ from the username limit?
items.expected_answer: Passwords may be at most 128 characters; usernames at most 64.

items.question: How many failed login attempts trigger a lockout, and how long does the lockout window last?
items.expected_answer: 5 failed attempts, with a 300 second lockout window.

items.question: How many customers reported being charged twice, and for which order IDs?
items.expected_answer: Two customers, for orders ORD-551884 and ORD-552088.

items.question: What was the most frequently reported problem across these tickets?
items.expected_answer: Checkout/payment hanging then failing with an error, without the card being charged.
